en: One fascicle of the *Nakṣatra-vidhi* (Ritual Manual of the Constellations), composed by Yi-hang.
The Seal of Ākāśagarbha: Form the *añjali* mudrā; bind the fingers of the water-element (*ap*) and shape the wind-element (*vāyu*) fingers like a jewel. The mantra:
It is said:
Oṃ agasa karape iya oṃ marī gamarī muri svāhā. If a person desires to seek merit and wisdom, [they should recite this].
One should take refuge in this Bodhisattva;
for the sun, moon,
and stars are all transformations produced by Gaganagañja.
The Mañjuśrī Seal: Join the palms in the "space" gesture (*ākāśa-muṣṭi*).
Press each thumb against the two phalanges of the ring fingers.
Bend the two middle fingers and join their tips at the center of the palms.
The mantra is: Oṃ āḥ jvālā hūṃ khacaraḷa. If one seeks pacification and desires to eliminate the seven kinds of calamities, [one should recite this].
That which is called the eclipsing of the sun and moon;
the five planets deviating from their regular courses;
and the concurrent uprising of armies and bandits.
Floods and droughts occur out of season, and wind and rain fall in violation of their proper measure.
Wicked ministers act in rebellion and cause harm to the people.
Fierce and predatory beasts devour living beings.
Should the five grains fail to ripen,
or should such calamities, urgent perils, troubles with government officials, royal difficulties, or fears of death occur—
they shall all be dispersed and vanish.
The Samantabhadra Seal: Joining the palms with the hollowed heart, the mantra is recited as follows:
*Cibbaṭa* (1), *niyambhaṭa* (2), *chindhi osarabhaṭa* (3). This mantra should be recited seven times at dawn and seven times at night.
Malevolent enchantments, wild paths, insects, and poisons will all be completely extinguished.
One will be able to attain the three liberations of body,
mind, and wisdom, and in future lives, one will not receive a body subject to birth and death.
One attains the Dharma-body. Upon hearing the sound of this mantra, all internal and external lands,
enemies and bandits, all evil persons, all ghosts and spirits, all thieves, tigers, wolves, lions, poisonous insects, and malevolent beasts [shall be subdued].
All shall have their mouths sealed shut so as not to disturb or confuse one another;
celestial portents, calamities, evil dreams, and misfortunes,
as well as the strange anomalies of the hundred birds, shall naturally vanish away.
The efficacy of this mantra cannot be fully described.
For the Life-Extending Seal (*āyur-vardhana-mudrā*): with the left hand, form the *vajrāñjali* and extend the index finger like a lotus flower.
Extend the right hand straight down as if hanging.
The mantra is: Oṃ mañjari svāhā. If one recites this mantra, it will prolong life and eliminate calamities.
The Seal of Śakra-devendra: The right hand forms a fist placed at the waist;
the left hand is held upright with the fingers touching one another;
the second and third fingers (the earth and water fingers) are bent at their middle joints.
Place the wind finger upon the back of the fire finger and bend the middle joint of the space finger.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ indrāya svāhā. If one recites this mantra and bestows it upon another, they will be granted official rank and their aspirations will be fulfilled.
The mudrā of Vaiśravaṇa: join the palms with the fingers hollowed out.
The two *śūnyatā* [elements] intersect and stand upright;
the two *vāyu* [elements] are attached to the sides of the two *tejas* [elements].
Like the tips of hooks, they are separated by one *cun* and do not touch.
The mantra is: Oṃ vaiśravaṇāya svāhā. If one recites this mantra, one will obtain great wealth and abundance, and [the deity] will provide protection day and night.
The mantra of the Sun is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo sūryāya sarvanakṣatrarājāya, oṃ amogha-ūrjaviśati svāhā*. The mantra of the Moon is as follows:
Oṃ jvalanatara-jvalarāja nāma sthite svāhā. This is the mantra of the Fire Star (Aṅgāraka).
Oṃ agāruṇiye nāma svāhā. The mantra of Mercury is:
Oṃ budhanakṣatramitre nāma kinnu mahe svāhā. The mantra of Jupiter is: Oṃ... [as above].
Oṃ bharasapatti namo bidavanase nāma-ma-lavara dhāne svāhā. The mantra of the planet Venus (Śukra) is as follows: [Oṃ bharasapatti namo bidavanase nāma-malavaradhāne svāhā].
Oṃ śukragrahadhāraṇarājāya svāhā. The mantra of Saturn (Śanaiścara) is: Oṃ śaniścarāṅgārakabṛhaspataye svāhā. The mantra of Rāhu is: [Oṃ rāhave svāhā].
Oṃ rāhukāsura-rāja-samasta-dunāmne śāntikari svāhā. The mantra of the planet Ketu is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-hetu-nakṣatra-rāja svāhā. (9) The mudrā of the planetary deities (*graha*) is: the firm *añjali* gesture.
The two empty forms stand side by side and upright;
the two winds expand,
which is called the fundamental opening and establishing of coming and going.
The mantra is: Oṃ a-ra-hi-sva-ri-ya pra-pra-ta ju-ṭi ma-ya svāhā. The mudrā of the twenty-eight lunar mansions: join the palms firmly.
Place both thumbs upright against the heart;
summon [the deity] with both thumbs.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña svāhā. First, offer this to the Bodhisattvas and devas, including Ākāśagarbha, Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Jīvita-Indra, Vaiśravaṇa, and others.

Thereafter, he offered petitions to the Nine Luminaries, the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions, the Celestial Beidou (Northern Dipper), the natal star to which one belongs, as well as the Lord of Mount Tai, Siming, and Silu.
I pray for the removal of calamities, the prolongation of life, and the elimination of misfortunes and harms.
The mantra for auspiciousness is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo samyak-saṃbuddha-nirjāta-āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā: anumate prānumate sabhini khe svāhā.* Recite this Great White-Robed Avalokiteśvara Dhāraṇī for the pacification of the nine planets.
If the sun or moon enters one’s natal mansion (*janmanakṣatra*),
or if the five planets enter the natal mansion and engage in conflict or lose their proper course,
one may establish a ritual site (*maṇḍala*) for Mahāpāṇḍaravāsini Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, or the Eight-Character *Cintāmaṇicakra* or the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā*.
Recite each according to its own respective ritual method;
all calamities will naturally dissipate,
and all inauspicious planetary influences will become auspicious through the recitation of this mantra.
The mantra of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper is as follows:
Oṃ saptānarcirya-bhañja-mi-rañjita-maṇḍala-svamin-namitara-kiṃśan-bhava-tu svāhā. If Rāhu or Ketu afflict a person’s natal star mansion, [recite this].
One must recite this mantra of the Northern Dipper,
as taught by all the Tathāgatas;
it brings auspiciousness by destroying all obstacles caused by the lunar mansions and planets.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvvanakṣatrasamaye śrīye śāntikakuru svāhā. From the *Vajranakṣatra-siddhi-sūtra*.
The Chapter on the Accomplishment of Auspiciousness states:
"I shall now proclaim the wondrous secret methods for accomplishing worldly aims.
Thus do the various planetary deities traverse the void."
Whether it be one, two, three, four, five, or more [days],

when the life-constellation (*jātakarṇa*) of a person about to enter the assembly is in opposition to their natal constellation (*janmanakṣatra*), or during the constellation of transmigration (*saṃkrāntinakṣatra*), the constellation of great slaughter (*mahāvadha-karmanakṣatra*), the constellation of peace (*śāntanakṣatra*), the constellation of meager fortune (*durbhagā-nakṣatra*), or the constellation of slaves and servants (*dāsī-dāsa-nakṣatra*).
They inflict various calamities and harms.
Among the four great malevolent planets—
namely Mars, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu— they are the most grievous to sentient beings.
At that time, one should cultivate various meritorious deeds and extensively practice benevolence and compassion;
either by relying on the Eight-Syllable Mantra of Mañjuśrī,
or by relying on the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Buddha-Crown.
Either relying on the Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara or the Ekākṣarorājā Uṣṇīṣa,
one establishes a great homa altar for pacifying calamities.
Recite the mantras and perform the offerings according to each respective root ritual;
all calamities will naturally be extinguished.
To perform the rite of accomplishment, one should do so on days when the Heart (Hṛdayā), the Willow (Jyeṣṭhā), the Pleiades (Mṛgaśiras), or the Ox (Vṛṣabha) lunar mansions are in conjunction.
Without distinguishing between the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of days or months,
one should simply perform this on a day when the lunar mansion (nakṣatra) is favorable; during that single day,
one should refrain from eating and recite [the mantra] one thousand and eighty times.
All heart-wishes shall be fulfilled immediately, and one will attain great *siddhi*.
In times of calamity and distress,
this is most efficacious on one's own birthday.
If one performs the rite of accomplishment for Jupiter (wood-day),
the sixteenth day of the month is most appropriate.
If one performs the rite of accomplishment for Mars (fire-day),...
That specific day of the week is most appropriate;
if one performs the rite of accomplishment for Saturn,
the seventh day of each month is most appropriate.
If one performs the rite of accomplishment for Venus (Śukra),
it is most appropriate to do so at dawn, facing whichever direction one perceives.
If one performs the rite of accomplishment for Mercury (Budha), one should perform the accomplishment on the day when Mercury is the presiding planet.
If one performs the rites for Rāhu or Ketu,
they should correspond to the time of one's own birth.
Furthermore, if one makes offerings to one's natal star, [the same applies].
If one attains accomplishment on the anniversary of one's birth year or the day of one's birth,
one should perform monthly offerings if one was born under an inauspicious constellation.
If one performs offerings for three days or seven days, it will immediately transform into auspiciousness itself.
Keep this secret and do not let the laity know.
*Suyao yigui* (Ritual Manual of Planets and Constellations), one fascicle.
